title: Adaptive client connection pooling and checkpointed pagination: PRD & acceptance criteria
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Problem: Large result sets and noisy networks cause client libraries to open excessive connections and lose progress when a streaming or paginated operation fails mid-flight. Users implementing long-running exports or bulk reads currently need to build custom retry+cursor logic and manage sockets independently, which leads to inefficiency, duplicated code, and poor UX across Python/TS/Go SDKs.

Objective: Define client SDK requirements that standardize adaptive connection pooling and checkpointed pagination so: (1) clients reuse connections efficiently across concurrent logical iterators, (2) paginated and streaming reads expose compact, forward-compatible checkpoints that allow exact resumption without re-fetching already-processed items, and (3) the behavior is consistent across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs with clear downgrade/deprecation rules for older client versions.

Scope: Platform and client-surface requirements for SDKs supporting Redwood API paginated endpoints and server-streaming endpoints. Deliverables: PRD, API contract (cursor/checkpoint format), deterministic resume semantics, client-side connection pool algorithm, test matrix, compatibility rules, and acceptance criteria.

Out of scope: Server-side changes to pagination semantics beyond checkpoint token addition, GUI/Console UX changes, billing model changes, and private deployment installation instructions.
user_stories: As a backend engineer using Redwood SDK, I want a resumable iterator over a large collection so my job can resume from the last checkpoint after a transient network failure without double-processing items.
As an infra engineer running high-concurrency workloads, I want the SDK to automatically reuse and limit connections so we don't exhaust client-side sockets under heavy fanout.
As an SDK maintainer, I want a single contract for checkpoint encoding that survives minor server model changes so we can evolve the server without breaking older clients.
As a TypeScript frontend developer, I want predictable cancellation and backpressure behavior when streaming so I can implement graceful shutdowns and progress bars.
As a Go service, I want the default pool sizing to be conservative but tunable so ephemeral functions (short-lived) don't induce high socket churn.
requirements: Checkpoint token: opaque, base64url-encoded JSON blob containing: server_cursor, last_seen_id, sequence_offset, protocol_version. Clients must not parse fields except opaque storage and signature verification for tamper detection.

Resume semantics: resume(checkpoint) must guarantee non-duplication for idempotent processing by default; semantics are 'at-least-once-safe' with an explicit flag for 'no-overlap' that server will attempt but cannot guarantee under replication edge cases.

Connection pooling: SDKs must provide a shared connection pool per process/container with conservative defaults (min=1, max=16) and an adaptive window that grows linearly under steady throughput until tokenized cost or latency SLO triggers a shrink.
Per-iterator affinity: iterators may optionally pin to a connection (configurable) to reduce KV-cache misses on the server; default behavior is best-effort connection reuse without pinning.

Backoff & retry: exponential backoff with jitter for transient network errors, with per-operation retry budget; streaming reads should checkpoint progress before retrying to avoid re-processing large batches.
Streaming cancellation: Abort/cancel must close logical iterator and return the latest checkpoint synchronously where possible so callers can persist state immediately.

Cross-language contract: Python/TS/Go must expose the same high-level APIs (iterator/paginator, checkpoint API, pooled client) and consistent default parameters; naming may follow language idioms but semantics must match.

Compatibility: server will include 'protocol_version' in checkpoint; SDKs must decode protocol_version but fall back to safest resume behavior for unknown versions and surface a clear error advising upgrade when resume cannot be guaranteed.
Telemetry: SDKs must emit lightweight telemetry events: pool_resize, checkpoint_emitted, resume_attempt(success|failure), and pool_exhausted. Telemetry must be opt-out and respect PII rules.
non_goals: Do not change server-side pagination semantics beyond adding checkpoint metadata to responses.
Do not implement server-side sticky routing to specific GPU nodes as part of this ticket.
Do not ship per-tenant custom pool sizing defaults in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) provide a documented Paginator/Streamer API that exposes .checkpoint() and .resume(checkpoint) primitives.

Round-trip test: create an iterator, fetch N pages, persist checkpoint, simulate client restart, resume from checkpoint and verify no items < last_seen_id are returned (unit tests & integration tests).
Connection pool behavior validated under load test: with 200 concurrent logical iterators, pool does not spawn > 16 connections by default; test harness verifies adaptive growth and shrink behavior.

Compatibility test: A checkpoint produced by the server with protocol_version X can be resumed by SDKs implementing X and by older SDKs which must either resume safely or produce a clear informative error recommending an SDK upgrade.
Telemetry: events pool_resize and checkpoint_emitted appear in test telemetry sink for all three SDKs, and can be toggled off via opt-out config.
API docs and code samples for each language published in the SDK repos and referenced in a single PRD/Confluence page.
technical_notes:
- Checkpoint token must be HMAC-signed by server; clients must validate signature to detect accidental corruption but must treat signature failures as non-resumable and surface a user-facing error.
- Consider using shared HTTP/2 multiplexed connection where supported (TS/Python gRPC/http2 libs) to reduce per-connection overhead.
- For server-streaming endpoints that send incremental deltas, emit checkpoints at configurable byte/record thresholds to bound re-processing costs.
- Default pool sizing rationale: 1 connection for low concurrency + heuristic growth to 16 for high throughput containers; document how to tune in serverless environments.
- Edge-case: if client persists checkpoint after processing but before server ack of last page, resume may re-deliver a small set; include idempotency guidance in samples.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): Shipping SDK primitives and tests in experimental feature flag across SDKs; enable for 10% of accounts in hosted environment. Phase 2: Collect telemetry, iterate on defaults and retry budgets. Phase 3: GA with docs, migration guide, and console dashboard of checkpointed exports. Target GA: 2026-04-15.
risks: Misunderstanding of opaque checkpoint: some teams may be tempted to parse server-internal fields — risk of breakage if server changes internal shape.
Pool heuristics may be suboptimal for extreme serverless short-lived processes (cold-start churn).
Cross-language subtle differences (e.g., Node HTTP/2 vs Go net/http2) may produce different connection reuse characteristics that frustrate customers.
